questions.q: What was the actual root cause confirmed behind the 3 AM alert?
options: A malicious actor exploited a software vulnerability on the jump host
The vendor remote-support firewall rule was scoped to 198.51.0.0/16 instead of the vendor's real 198.51.100.16/28, and had been since the rule's creation
The Conditional Access pilot policy was misconfigured
The correlation rule from Lesson 5 had a logic error
questions.explain: The root cause was a firewall rule scope mismatch present since the rule's original creation, not a vulnerability, CA issue, or correlation rule bug.

questions.q: What two kinds of tests validated the fix?
options: A unit test and an integration test
A positive test confirming the vendor's real connection still works, and a negative test confirming the old broad range is now denied
A load test and a stress test
A single test confirming the rule was deleted
questions.explain: Both a positive and a negative test were required to validate the scope correction.

questions.q: What two things changed as a result of this incident?
options: Nothing changed beyond the one rule edit
The firewall rule's scope was corrected, and a two-part standing control (per-change gate plus periodic review) was added to the process going forward
The vendor relationship was terminated
The correlation rule from Lesson 5 was removed
questions.explain: One change was technical (the rule's scope); the other was procedural (the new standing control).

questions.q: Why does the lesson describe this incident's failure mode as realistic rather than contrived?
options: Because it involves a sophisticated zero-day exploit
Because a vendor access rule written too broadly under deadline pressure and never reviewed afterward is a common, ordinary real cause of unintended exposure
Because it required an insider threat
Because it only happens in utility companies
questions.explain: The lesson explicitly frames this as deliberately ordinary -- the kind of problem a working analyst actually finds -- rather than a dramatic breach scenario.

questions.q: What does the Advanced tier build on top of, according to this lesson?
options: An entirely unrelated scenario with no connection to this project
This project's same discipline -- tracing alerts to root cause, validating fixes, turning incidents into standing controls -- carried forward toward a board-level security review
A rebuild of the Beginner project from scratch
Only new firewall vendor products, with no process carried forward
questions.explain: The Advanced tier is built separately but carries this project's discipline forward toward a board-level review, without this lesson describing its specific content.
